shortcut_name: involutory matrix reduction to bipartite coloring
evidence: deepseek uses "color[start] = 0  # mode 1" and alternates colors; gpt-oss labels its array "0 / 1 bipartite colour"; qwen explicitly implements "matrix_power" and matrix equality; glm builds a binary "color" assignment with BFS.
affordance_in_statement: Each instance has M_i = ((3, -4), (2, -3))^{s_i}, and every shared pair must satisfy C_{u,v} = M_u × M_v != I.
removal_suggestion: Replace or re-present the fixed transformation so that its powers do not make M_u M_v equal I exactly when the two modes are equal. In particular, avoid exposing an involutory matrix whose square is the identity; use a non-involutory mode transformation or a genuinely mode-dependent transformation instead.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the constraints as a two-color graph and assigns alternating modes by BFS.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The matrix is an involution, so a pair is invalid exactly when both endpoints receive the same mode.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a 0/1 bipartite-color array and converts it to modes 1/2.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The identity-product constraint reduces to requiring opposite colors on every edge.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Computes the matrix powers/products, then relies on the resulting two-color constraint.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The explicitly supplied matrix satisfies A^2 = I, making equal modes produce the forbidden identity product.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Runs BFS with binary colors to construct the mode assignment.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The matrix condition is equivalent to a graph bipartiteness condition.

common_affordance: The supplied base matrix is an involution: A^2 = I, so M_u M_v = I exactly when the two endpoint modes are equal, reducing the whole problem to bipartite graph coloring.
recommended_edit: Change the fixed transformation matrix or its presentation so that A^2 is not the identity and the forbidden product is no longer equivalent to equal endpoint modes; this removes the shared bipartite-coloring shortcut from all four solutions.
